edges.description: Near-universal in this tumour and reported to suppress p53 signalling through MDM4, but no cited source shows it causes the tumour, and it occurs in other FOXR2-overexpressing brain tumours as well.

nodes.description: FOXR2 is a forkhead transcription factor on the X chromosome whose expression in normal postnatal human tissue is restricted to the testis. In this tumour it is expressed in brain. The parallel the literature draws is with cancer-testis antigen genes, which sit on the X chromosome, are normally confined to the testis, and escape silencing through hypomethylation; promoter hypomethylation is described as the predominant regulatory mechanism, with structural variation the other route.

nodes.description: A supratentorial brain tumour of young children, median age around five years in the largest cohort and 4.2 years in two others, almost always in the cerebral hemispheres. A slight female predominance is reported.

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic implications of improved molecular diagnostics for rare CNS embryonal tumor entities: results of an international, retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Median age at diagnosis was 5.0 years (range 1.0-20.0 years), and sex ratio was nearly balanced with 56/102 females (55%) (Figure 2B, C). Tumor location was supratentorial in all 87 cases with available information (Figure 2D).

nodes.description: Gain of chromosome arm 1q is present in nearly every tumour, 43 of 44 in the defining series and 94 to 100 per cent in later cohorts, alongside frequent 16q loss and 17q gain. It has been reported to converge on suppression of p53 signalling through MDM4 overexpression. It is not specific: 1q gain was found in 70.6 per cent of high-grade gliomas overexpressing FOXR2, so neither 1q gain nor FOXR2 overexpression identifies this entity on its own.

evidence.reference_title: New Brain Tumor Entities Emerge from Molecular Classification of CNS-PNETs.
evidence.snippet: Gain of chromosome arm 1q was characteristic for the CNS NB-FOXR2 entity (43/44, 98 %; p < 0.001)

evidence.reference_title: FOXR2 activation is not exclusive of CNS neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Chromosome arm 1q gain (1q+), a characteristic molecular alteration of CNS NB-FOXR2, was seen in 70.6% (12/17) of HGGs with FOXR2 overexpression tested, demonstrating that the combination of 1q+ and FOXR2 overexpression is not specific to CNS NB-FOXR2.

nodes.description: The best-documented approach is upfront craniospinal irradiation with chemotherapy. In the largest cohort, 35 of 42 progression-free survivors had received it, five-year progression-free and overall survival were 63 and 85 per cent, and the authors attribute the favourable outcome to the use of craniospinal irradiation, noting a higher recurrence rate in patients who were not irradiated or were irradiated locally. They propose that a standard-risk craniospinal irradiation regimen be evaluated prospectively, which has not yet been done. Late relapses occur, the latest at 5.9 years, so follow-up has to be long.

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic implications of improved molecular diagnostics for rare CNS embryonal tumor entities: results of an international, retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Best treatment results were achieved for CNS NB-FOXR2 patients (5-year PFS: 63% ± 7%, OS: 85% ± 5%, n = 63), with 35/42 progression-free survivors after upfront craniospinal irradiation (CSI) and chemotherapy.

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic implications of improved molecular diagnostics for rare CNS embryonal tumor entities: results of an international, retrospective study.

nodes.description: The tumour that results is an embryonal neoplasm showing foci of neuroblastic or neuronal differentiation, which is what the World Health Organization's essential diagnostic criteria require alongside FOXR2 activation or a matching methylation profile. Morphology alone does not make the diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: The essential diagnostic criteria of the WHO classification defines NB-FOXR2 as an embryonal tumor having foci of neuroblastic or neuronal differentiation and a FOXR2 activation or a DNA-methylation profile aligned with this diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: In accordance with the WHO Classification, our work evidenced that a diagnosis of NB-FOXR2 based on morphology alone is currently not possible.

nodes.description: Somatic structural variants clustering within roughly 150 kb upstream of FOXR2 on Xp11.21: interchromosomal translocations, tandem duplications, inversions, deletions, a mitochondrial DNA insertion creating a novel promoter, and truncated LINE-1 retrotransposition. They are varied in kind and consistent in position. Crucially they spare the coding region, so there need be no chimeric protein and no fusion transcript, and routine testing can miss them.

evidence.reference_title: New Brain Tumor Entities Emerge from Molecular Classification of CNS-PNETs.
evidence.snippet: Genome-wide sequencing revealed complex inter- and intrachromosomal re-arrangements converging on forkhead box R2 (FOXR2) in 6/8 samples with available data, leading to increased FOXR2 gene expression levels in CNS NB-FOXR2 tumors compared with other CNS tumor entities

evidence.reference_title: FOXR2-activated CNS neuroblastoma: Characterized by variable structural disruption of the FOXR2 regulatory region, recurrent copy number alterations, and elevated FOXR2 expression.
evidence.snippet: Despite this variability, all breakpoints appear to be consistently located within approximately 150 kb upstream of FOXR2, a regulatory zone that is vulnerable to genomic disruptions leading to FOXR2 activation.

evidence.reference_title: FOXR2-activated CNS neuroblastoma: Characterized by variable structural disruption of the FOXR2 regulatory region, recurrent copy number alterations, and elevated FOXR2 expression.
evidence.snippet: Importantly, these structural alterations do not affect the coding region of FOXR2 and may not result in RNA fusion transcripts or chimeric proteins. Instead, FOXR2 overexpression may occur through mechanisms such as promoter hijacking, which require direct assessment of gene expression.

nodes.description: Resection is the first local treatment. Extent varies and is reported rather than prescribed: gross total resection was achieved in 7 of 10 patients by first or second resection in one cohort, and in a small series two patients had gross total and two subtotal resection. No cited source compares outcomes by extent of resection in this entity, so the entry records practice and not a benefit.
